strengths: The core insight of replacing a globally fused 3D memory (which accumulates registration and depth errors) with multiple clean, retrieved per-frame local geometric memories is clever and highly effective for long-horizon generation.
The coverage-driven memory retrieval algorithm is well-formulated, greedily selecting complementary memories to maximize visibility coverage and avoid redundant conditioning signals.

The multi-anchor weaving controller, utilizing shared cross-anchor attention and camera-pose-guided fusion, successfully and learnably resolves residual misalignment across different retrieved local views.

Strong quantitative and qualitative results on RealEstate10K and DL3DV datasets, outperforming state-of-the-art camera-controllable and memory-augmented baselines across both reconstruction and perceptual metrics.
The paper is exceptionally well-structured and written, with extensive ablation studies, clear architectural figures, and comprehensive visual evaluations.
weaknesses: The computational and memory overhead is a concern. Jointly processing $K$ anchor videos in the shared multi-anchor attention block scales up the sequence length ($1 	imes K \cdot L_a$). An analysis of the extra GPU memory footprint, inference speed, and rendering overhead compared to single-anchor or global-memory approaches is missing.

The method remains heavily reliant on the performance of the external test-time 3D reconstruction model (TTT3R) for estimating per-frame geometry and camera poses. A discussion on how the model behaves under highly inaccurate or noisy single-view depth estimates would strengthen the work.

Handling of dynamic scenes is limited. While the authors showcase a gaming example by masking out the dynamic character, the underlying representation (rigid camera poses and static point clouds) is fundamentally designed for static scenes, making it less applicable to environments with complex object motions.

strengths: Well-motivated key insight: Replacing a single, error-prone global 3D model with multiple clean local point cloud memories is a highly effective way to prevent the accumulation and propagation of cross-view alignment errors during multi-view fusion.

Well-designed technical components: The coverage-driven retrieval strategy successfully selects a non-redundant, complementary set of anchors, while the Multi-Anchor Weaving Controller leverages shared attention and pose-guided fusion to elegantly reconcile residual geometric inconsistencies.

Comprehensive and solid experimental evaluation: The paper compares against a wide range of strong baselines (such as SPMem, SEVA, and ViewCrafter) across both DL3DV and RealEstate10K, showing noticeable improvements in both reconstruction accuracy (PSNR, SSIM) and perceptual metrics.

Impressive long-term consistency and generalization: The qualitative results for open-domain scenes, 360-degree camera rotations, and character-masked dynamic video generation highlight the robustness of the system over long horizons.
weaknesses: Computational overhead and efficiency concerns: Managing multiple local point clouds, performing greedy coverage-driven retrieval, rendering up to K=4 anchors, and passing multiple anchor videos through ControlNet blocks with shared cross-attention is computationally expensive. The paper lacks a quantitative analysis of inference latency, GPU memory usage, and rendering overhead compared to single-anchor methods.

Heavy dependency on external 3D estimation: The framework relies on high-quality frame-level pose and depth estimation (using TTT3R). If the monocular estimation fails (e.g., in textureless areas, reflections, or repeating patterns), it remains unclear how gracefully the Multi-Anchor Weaving Controller handles severely degraded geometry.

Under-detailed retrieval and pose-guided fusion implementation: The paper does not fully explain how the visibility coverage maximization is implemented (e.g., whether it uses z-buffering or point splatting, and its runtime). Additionally, the exact input representation for the relative camera poses in the pose-aware MLP should be clarified.

strengths: Intuitive and well-motivated approach: The paper correctly identifies that globally fusing point clouds accumulates registration and pose estimation errors over long horizons, leading to ghosting artifacts. Replacing global fusion with retrieved per-frame local spatial memories and learning to reconcile their residual inconsistencies is a very logical and elegant solution.

Well-designed technical components: The coverage-driven memory retrieval, formulated as a visibility coverage maximization problem, is sound. The Multi-anchor Weaving Controller effectively fuses the anchors using shared multi-anchor attention (for cross-view information exchange) and pose-guided fusion (to weight anchors by viewpoint proximity).

Rigorous experimental validation: The authors compare against a comprehensive set of state-of-the-art baselines on RealEstate10K and DL3DV datasets. For a fair comparison, non-open-sourced methods (such as SPMem and Context-as-Memory) are carefully reimplemented on the same CogVideoX backbone.

Strong qualitative and generalization results: The long-horizon, 360-degree rotation, and free-form camera trajectory results on open-domain scenes demonstrate highly stable geometric and appearance consistency, and the extension to dynamic third-person character scenes showcases robust generalization.
weaknesses: Lack of discussion on computational and memory complexity: Storing per-frame local point clouds scales linearly with the length of the generated environment. Furthermore, rendering up to K=4 anchor videos, encoding them through the VAE, and performing joint attention over multiple concatenated sequences must introduce non-trivial overhead. Quantitative metrics regarding inference speed (FPS) and GPU memory consumption during training and generation should be provided.

Potential boundary artifacts across temporal chunks: In Sec 3.3, memory retrieval is done independently for temporal chunks of length D, and the rendered anchors are concatenated. Because different chunks might retrieve different sets of local memories, there could be sudden transitions in the conditioning anchors at chunk boundaries. Clarification on how the model maintains smooth transitions and avoids boundary flickering/discontinuities is needed.

Reliance on external 3D estimators: The performance of the framework is heavily dependent on the accuracy of the external 3D estimator (e.g., TTT3R) for depth and camera poses. An analysis or discussion of failure cases when these estimators perform poorly (e.g., in highly textureless, dark, or reflective scenes) would make the manuscript more complete.

strengths: Innovative and well-motivated concept: Replacing globally fused 3D memory (which accumulates drift and alignment errors) with multiple clean, view-aligned local 3D memories is a highly effective and clever solution for long-horizon consistent video generation.

Comprehensive and well-engineered system design: The proposed coverage-driven retrieval pipeline and the multi-anchor weaving controller (employing shared multi-anchor attention and pose-guided fusion) are technically sound and elegantly address the challenges of multi-view conditioning.

Extensive and rigorous experimental validation: The paper compares against a wide array of state-of-the-art baselines on two challenging datasets (RealEstate10K, DL3DV) using two different modern DiT backbones (CogVideoX and Wan2.2). It achieves impressive results across both reconstruction and perceptual metrics.

Outstanding ablation studies and diagnostics: The analyses—such as the global vs. local memory diagnostic, the long-horizon stress test of 2400 frames, and the runtime scaling behavior—are thorough, highly informative, and clearly demonstrate the benefits of the proposed method.
weaknesses: Computational overhead of multi-anchor processing: Processing K=4 anchor video streams increases both generation time (by ~24% compared to K=1) and GPU memory consumption (from 34GB to 39GB). While the history-length scaling is better than global fusion approaches, the absolute overhead of the controller is still non-trivial.

Heavy reliance on external monocular 3D estimation: The performance is bound by the quality of the upstream monocular 3D reconstruction model (e.g., TTT3R). In cases of textureless regions, non-Lambertian surfaces, or out-of-distribution scenes, errors in pose and depth estimation will still propagate into the local memories.

Minor lack of detail on relative pose representation: The manuscript does not explicitly specify the parameterization format of the retrieved-to-target relative camera poses (e.g., matrix representation, translation + quaternions, etc.) used as inputs to the MLP for pose-guided fusion.

strengths: Well-motivated approach that addresses the standard failure mode of global 3D memory fusion (drift, alignment noise, and ghosting) by utilizing clean, individual local memories.
The coverage-driven memory retrieval algorithm provides a systematic way to select the most informative and complementary views along a target camera trajectory.
The design of the Multi-anchor Weaving Controller is technically sound, employing shared attention and pose-guided fusion to robustly handle residual geometric inconsistencies.
Thorough experimental evaluation and extensive ablation studies in both the main paper and appendix, including long-horizon stress tests (up to 2400 frames) and scaling analyses.
weaknesses: High computational and memory overhead: Maintaining per-frame local point clouds instead of a unified global model increases storage and indexing requirements. Additionally, rendering multiple anchor videos ($K=4$) and processing them through a multi-branch controller adds significant inference time and GPU memory usage.

Marginal quantitative improvement over strong baselines: As shown in Table 1, the proposed method's reconstruction performance (e.g., PSNR of 21.04 for AnchorWeave Wan2.2-5B vs. 21.13 for SEVA) is highly comparable or slightly lower than existing methods like SEVA, indicating that the quantitative margin is tight.

Heavy reliance on external 3D estimation: The accuracy of the rendering-based conditioning depends entirely on the camera poses and depth maps estimated by external models (like TTT3R). In textureless, reflective, or highly dynamic scenes where these estimators fail, the quality of the generated video will degrade significantly.

Limited capability for complex dynamic environments: The core framework is designed around static scene representations. While character masking is proposed in the appendix as a workaround, it is a heuristic and does not offer a unified solution for general dynamic world modeling (e.g., objects changing shape, moving, or lighting variations).

strengths: Highly intuitive and elegant core concept: replacing a noisy globally fused 3D memory representation with a collection of clean, view-aligned local 3D memories, shifting the reconciliation of viewpoint inconsistencies to a learnable joint-attention controller.

Well-designed technical components, including the greedy visibility coverage maximization algorithm for memory retrieval, the joint cross-anchor attention mechanism, and the pose-guided fusion module that weights anchors by viewpoint proximity.

Comprehensive and rigorous experimental evaluation. The paper benchmarks against a wide range of state-of-the-art camera-controllable and memory-augmented video generators, including re-implementations of non-open-source baselines on identical backbones.

Thorough diagnostic analyses, such as the long-horizon stress test (up to 2400 frames), scaling of retrieval/rendering costs with respect to history frames, and detailed ablations of each proposed design choice.
The manuscript is extremely well-written, with high-quality illustrations and clear mathematical formulations.
weaknesses: Increased inference-time computational overhead. Processing multiple local anchors ($K=4$) increases generation time and GPU memory footprint during diffusion denoising compared to single-anchor methods.

Strong reliance on the accuracy of the underlying 3D pose/depth estimator. Although multi-view fusion drift is avoided, severe failures in per-frame monocular depth or pose estimation in highly out-of-distribution or textureless environments can still degrade output quality.

The framework is fundamentally designed for static backgrounds. Handling dynamic content (e.g., characters) currently requires pre-processing steps like masking them out during point-cloud construction.
